title: Annotatio IV §.II: Institution shows presence and participation — special Mode from Christ & Paul
english: Institution words clearly enough hint presence and participation of body and blood — but decide nothing about the special Mode of either.
That whole Mode must be sought from Christ’s and Paul’s discourses as the only, fullest, most lucid commentaries.

title: Annotatio IV §.II: Dispute on John 6 — is it about the Lord’s Supper? Both sides true
english: Long sharp fight even within the same Christian camp: does John 6 treat the Lord’s Supper and sacramental eating/drinking of Christ’s flesh and blood?
Some yes, some no — both sides can be true once the dispute is composed.

title: Annotatio IV §.II cont.: Not full (no bread/wine) but semi-full (flesh eaten / blood drunk)
english: Supper-talk can be full (the whole) or semi-full (a part). John 6 is not full: no Eucharistic bread and wine, which are essential integrating parts of the sacrament.
It is semi-full: it does treat eating flesh and drinking blood — the Supper’s chief nearest object and the commanded sacramental action.

title: Annotatio IV §.II: John 6 = antecedent most lucid commentary on the Institution words
english: So read, John 6 specially exposes what the sacramental Mode of presence and participation is — the antecedent, most lucid commentary on the Institution words.
Not on a Supper already instituted then, but on the one soon to be: torch and light for ‘This is my Body’ / ‘This is my blood,’ clearing the disciples’ scruples.

title: Annotatio IV §.II close: Mode merely Spiritual / Supernatural / Celestial — stop before §.III
english: That Mode of presence and participation is merely Spiritual, Supernatural, Celestial.
It stands against corporal, natural, carnal, local presence — Capernaite in greater or lesser degree.
Stop before §.III (four proofs that John 6 inculcates the spiritual mode).

title: Annotatio IV §.III open: Four proofs that John 6 inculcates Spiritual / Supernatural / Celestial Mode
english: §.III: four proofs that in John 6 Christ inculcates the Spiritual, Supernatural, Celestial Mode of presence and participation of His body and blood.
Not any other mode — certainly not the Corporal, Natural, Earthly one.

title: Annotatio IV §.III (1): Presence whose partakers come by spiritual access — true living faith
english: (1) The only presence of body, blood, and whole Christ that is recommended is the one we share by spiritual access — true living faith (John 6:35, 47–51).
By that faith we partake spiritually rather than corporally — even outside the Sacred Supper.

title: Annotatio IV §.III (2): Spiritual effects follow only spiritual presence — not corporal or oral
english: (2) The presence and participation recommended are those which spiritual union with Christ, eternal life, and the last-day raising infallibly follow (John 6:53–56).
Those heavenly effects cling only to spiritual presence and participation — not corporal or oral; even on the Lutheran view the unworthy’s oral eating is spiritually empty.

title: Annotatio IV §.III (3): Mode compatible with ascension — Athanasius draws from corporal intellect
english: (3) The recommended presence must also stand with Christ’s bodily ascent into heaven (John 6:62) — so from the ascent one gathers spiritual presence on earth, not corporal.
Athanasius: He named the ascension to pull them off corporal intellect and teach His flesh as heavenly spiritual food. (Greek transliterated in Pass B.)

title: Annotatio IV §.III (4): Carnal / corporal participation profits nothing — Spiritus est qui vivificat
english: (4) Carnal or corporal participation of Christ’s flesh is of no use at all (John 6:63): the Spirit quickens; the flesh profits nothing; His words are spirit and life.

Augustine and Paschasius: without the Spirit neither flesh nor sacrament profits; Lutherans admit Christ without faith harms; Brentius: Capernaite tooth-tearing profits nothing — faith’s heart-teeth do.

title: Annotatio IV §.III close: Words Spirit and life — mystical nutrition; stop before §.IV (Pauline commentary)
english: Second half of (4): understand the flesh-and-blood words mystically and spiritually — Spirit and life — not as bodily food of a body-part, but spiritual nutrition joining members to the Head, eternal life and last-day raising.
Spiritually taken sense quickens; carnal coarse hearing profits nothing — why fasten a thick carnal sense on spiritual speech?
Stop before §.IV (antecedent Institution commentary hands off to the Pauline / Apostolic successor).

title: Annotatio IV §.IV open: Antecedent Institution commentary succeeded by Pauline 1 Cor. 10–11
english: §.IV: Christ’s antecedent Institution commentary (origin and foundation of the true sentence) is succeeded by the Apostolic / Pauline commentary — specially 1 Cor. 10 and 11.
Chapter 10 supplies many arguments for spiritual presence and participation of body and blood — none for the corporal.

title: Annotatio IV §.IV: First argument — OT spiritual food and drink; the Rock was Christ
english: First argument: OT believers already shared Christ’s communion — the same spiritual food and drink (1 Cor. 10:1–4); the Rock was Christ.
We NT Christians drink His blood spiritually and share the same spiritual food — Christ and His body — with the Fathers; signs differ, significata are the same (Augustine; Acts 15:11).

title: Annotatio IV §.IV cont.: Same significata; Petrus Martyr — death and flesh always present to God
english: Objection: how could ancients receive Christ sacramentally before flesh assumed and blood shed? Petrus Martyr: before God (and for faithful spiritual eating) death, blood-shedding, and flesh-assumption were always present and accepted — Lamb slain from the world’s foundation; Christ yesterday and forever; Abraham saw His day.

Flesh not yet in nature corporally could still save the Fathers spiritually; they held the Son by faith under promise of the nature to be assumed — we confess what they foresaw as already done. Martyr also answers two further specious objections solidly.

title: Annotatio IV §.IV: Second argument — cup and broken bread communion (1 Cor. 10:16–17) is spiritual
english: Second argument (1 Cor. 10:16–17): communion of the cup of blessing with Christ’s blood and of the broken bread with His body is like coalescing into one body as partakers of the one spiritual bread — Christ Himself.
That union into one body is not corporal but Spiritual.

title: Annotatio IV §.IV: Third & Fourth — Israel’s altar and Gentile demons: real spiritual communion
english: Third (v. 18): Israel’s sacrificers eating peace-offerings are partners of the altar with God — a spiritual, yet most real and substantial, communion.
Fourth (vv. 20–21): Gentile demon-sacrificers share the demons’ table — likewise spiritual, not corporal, yet real; Paul will not have us partners of demons.

title: Annotatio IV §.IV close: 1 Cor. 11 — Institution tropes; two things celestial & terrestrial; stop before §.V
english: 1 Cor. 11 chiefly founds the true Supper sentence: Paul repeats Institution from Christ’s mouth with emphasis — bread as body broken for us (v. 24); cup as the New covenant through His blood (v. 25) — tropical propositions, without denying spiritual presence and participation.
Vv. 26–28: the sacrament is two things, celestial and terrestrial, after consecration as before — bread and wine are not converted into body and blood; he keeps saying this bread / this cup.
Stop before §.V (Pauline true sentence lasting through the Apostolic first age).

title: Annotatio IV §.V open: Pauline true sentence endured through the Apostolic first age
english: §.V: the Pauline true Supper sentence — matching Institution and the John 6 antecedent commentary — lasted through the whole Apostolic first age.
All the Apostles and their disciples (Polycarp among them, John’s disciple) may fairly be read as approving it.

title: Annotatio IV §.V: Acts 2 — new converts devoted to Apostolic teaching and koinonia
english: Acts 2:42: Jews newly converted by Peter’s sermon — the first of all — kept attending assiduously (proskarterountes).
Not only to the Apostles’ teaching (didachē), including on the Supper, but also to the koinōnia Paul sets out in 1 Cor. 10:16–20.

title: Annotatio IV §.V cont.: Koinonia = spiritual communion with Christ and one another + bread-breaking
english: That koinōnia is spiritual communion with Christ and His body and blood, and among themselves.
Joined to it is the breaking of bread — always prefiguring the body broken for you (1 Cor. 11:24).

title: Annotatio IV §.V: First Christians’ koinonia with Apostles = communion with Father and Theanthropos Son — spiritual
english: So the first Christians’ koinōnia with the Apostles — and of every rightly communicating person through all ages — is at once communion with the heavenly Father and with His Son the God-man Jesus Christ (1 John 1:3), always to remain.
Yet it is Spiritual: Christ came not by water only but by water and blood.

title: Annotatio IV §.V: Spirit witnesses — Spirit is truth; Spirit quickens; words are Spirit and life
english: He did it so that the Spirit should bear witness that the Spirit is the truth (1 John 5:6 with John 6:63).
The Spirit is Truth; the Spirit quickens; Christ’s words on participating His Body and Blood are Spirit and life.

title: Annotatio IV §.V close: On to later ages via early Fathers; both sides cite two things, spiritual mode only — stop before §.VI
english: Doctrine now traced from the origin through the whole first Christian age — we may step on to later ages with early Fathers to confirm it.
Protestant collectors (Oecolampadius, Melanchthon, Chemnitz, Chamier, Cosin, Baier) already demolished Pontifical novelties; we still take two or three witnesses per purer age from them.

Both sides cite nearly the same from the first five ages: presence of two things (celestial & terrestrial / Signified & Sign) with only the spiritual mode of the Signified conceded. Stop before §.VI (second century: Ignatius, Justin, Irenaeus).

title: Annotatio IV §.VI open: Second century — Ignatius, Justin, Irenaeus on the true Eucharistic sentence
english: §.VI: in the SECOND Christian age after the Apostolic, the leading martyrs openly professed the true Eucharistic sentence from Christ and the Apostles.

Ignatius (start) turns the mind to the chief part held by faith alone; Justin (middle) to the lesser part not to be turned into the chief; Irenaeus (end) to both — presence, participation, and their mode.

title: Annotatio IV §.VI: Ignatius to Smyrna — Eucharist is the Savior’s flesh; Theodoret still cites it
english: Ignatius to the Smyrnaeans: the Eucharist is the Flesh of our Savior Jesus Christ, which suffered for our sins and which the Father raised.
Not to be written off as weak faith or among interpolated Ignatian writings — Theodoret in the fifth century still cites them in Dialogue 3 (apathēs / Impassible).

title: Annotatio IV §.VI: Justin Martyr — Eucharistic bread remains after consecration; Cosinus epiphonema
english: Justin (Apol. 2): after consecration the Eucharistic bread remains the same and feeds our flesh — no longer common, yet the food ‘changed’ that nourishes our flesh and blood we have learned is the flesh and blood of the incarnate Jesus.

Cosinus of Durham: therefore bread-substance remains after consecration as truly corruptible food — Christ’s immortal body does not nourish or change into our flesh; this food is sacramentally called Christ’s Flesh, which nourishes unto eternal life.

title: Annotatio IV §.VI: Irenaeus — Eucharist of two things, terrestrial and celestial (observations 1–2)
english: Irenaeus (Adv. Haer. 4.34) more fully: the Sacred Eucharist consists of two things — earthly and heavenly. Bread from earth receiving God’s invocation is no longer common bread but Eucharist.

(1) After consecration it is still bread, only severed from common use. (2) That separated bread is not itself Christ’s body as if transmuted — it is Eucharist: bread destined and consecrated for the sacrament.

title: Annotatio IV §.VI cont.: Irenaeus (3–4) — two things of the Eucharist; celestial = supernatural presence mode
english: (3) The two things belong to the Eucharist, not to the bread alone — lest Christ’s body be joined to bread even outside lawful use. (4) Earthly = bread from earth; heavenly is not Christ’s body naturally/corporally present (that body is an earthly thing from Mary’s mass, like us except sin).
It is called heavenly for the solely supernatural presence-mode in the Eucharist — genuine food of faithful souls from the Spirit, someday serving even their bodies toward blessed resurrection.

title: Annotatio IV §.VI close: Irenaeus Lib. 5 — nourished by creature, not natural body; stop before §.VII
english: Irenaeus Adv. Haer. 5.12: as wheat falls, dissolves, and rises manifold into Eucharist (body and blood of Christ), so faithful bodies nourished from it shall rise. We are nourished by the Creature He supplies — cup and bread as creature confirmed as His blood and Body.

When cup and bread receive God’s word there is made the Eucharist of His blood and body — not the blood and body themselves — from which our flesh’s substance increases. To say our bodies grow from Christ’s natural incorruptible body would be absurd and blasphemous.
Stop before §.VII (third century: Tertullian).

title: Annotatio IV §.VII open: Third century — Tertullian first professor of Eucharistic truth
english: §.VII opens the THIRD century with Tertullian as first professor of Eucharistic truth — in flower at the age’s start.
In one sentence he both confesses the impropriety of Christ’s words ‘This is my body’ and attests the true presence of Christ’s true body in the supper.

title: Annotatio IV §.VII: Tertullian Contra Marcionem — Hoc est corpus meum = figure of my body
english: Contra Marcionem 4.40: Christ made the bread taken and given to the disciples His Body by saying ‘This is my body’ — that is, the FIGURE OF MY BODY.
It would not be a figure unless it were a BODY OF TRUTH: an empty phantasm cannot take a figure.

title: Annotatio IV §.VII cont.: De Resurrectione Carnis nearly corporal — counted among his errors
english: Elsewhere (De Resurrectione Carnis) Tertullian seems to push a nearly corporal presence: our flesh is fed with Christ’s body and blood so the soul may be fattened from God.
Count that among his otherwise venerable errors — even Transsubstantiators wholly abhor proper nutrition of our flesh by Christ’s body taken in the supper.

title: Annotatio IV §.VII: Origen — impropriety and real presence; presence and participation merely spiritual
english: Next, Origen (same century): with Tertullian he stabilizes the impropriety of ‘This is my body’ and real presence — then urges that presence and participation are merely Spiritual.
Against Marcionites: if Christ had no flesh and blood, of what flesh and blood did He minister bread and cup as signs and IMAGES?

title: Annotatio IV §.VII cont.: Origen Hom. Lev. 7 — figures; spiritual not carnal; the letter kills
english: Origen Hom. Lev. 7: recognize they are figures — examine them as spiritual, not carnal; taken carnally they hurt and do not nourish.
The Gospel letter kills whoever does not hear spiritually: if you follow ‘Unless you eat my flesh and drink my blood’ according to the letter, that letter kills.

title: Annotatio IV §.VII close: Cyprian — invade the Lord’s body only spiritually; stop before §.VIII
english: Cyprian, later in the century, most expressly teaches true spiritual presence and participation — in rhetorical style (On the Lapsed) against the unprepared who still reek of idol foods yet invade the Lord’s Body.
They can invade Christ’s body and do violence to His blood only in a Spiritual mode — by taking bread and wine, which the impious handle only by sacrilege.
Stop before §.VIII (fourth century: Nicene Fathers).

title: Annotatio IV §.VIII open: Fourth century — Nicene Fathers’ complexus and the Marchic Reformed formula
english: §.VIII: stepping into the FOURTH century, first remember the Nicene Fathers’ complexus — opening the whole Church’s sentence on the Sacred Supper.

Our Marchic Reformed administration formula seems drawn from it: communicants must not cling to the sensed symbols, but lift the mind’s eyes to heaven and by divine faith hold that souls are fed by Christ’s true substantial body and blood no less than the mouth takes the symbols.

title: Annotatio IV §.VIII: Nicene words — lift the mind to heaven; Lamb of God; little for sanctification
english: Nicene words (Gelasius of Cyzicus / Scultetus): do not stay humble-eyed on the set bread and cup — by faith see the Lamb of God on that Table, truly receiving His precious body and Blood as symbols of our resurrection unto eternal life.
We take little, not much — not for satiety but for sanctification. Athanasius most exactly follows these Council footprints.

title: Annotatio IV §.VIII: Athanasius — spiritual presence and participation; exclude the corporal
english: Athanasius (on John 6) builds spiritual presence and participation of body and blood in the Supper — corporal presence and participation shut out.
The Lord separated Spirit from flesh so we know His speech is spiritual not carnal; He named the ascension to pull them off corporal intellect toward heavenly spiritual food (pneumatikēn trophēn).

title: Annotatio IV §.VIII cont.: Athanasius — heavenly spiritual food; Spirit and life distributed spiritually
english: ‘What I have spoken to you are Spirit and life’ — as if to say: my body shown and given for the world will be given as food so it is distributed to each spiritually (pneumatikōs).
It becomes for each a preservation unto the resurrection of eternal life.

title: Annotatio IV §.VIII: Ambrose — consecration’s change in the symbols is only spiritual
english: Ambrose (De Sacr. 4.4), late in the century, agrees: every change that consecration works in the Supper’s symbols is only spiritual.
You yourself were an old creature; after consecration you begin to be a new one. Ordinary bread before the blessing-words; when consecration comes, from bread is made Christ’s body.

title: Annotatio IV §.VIII close: Ambrose — after consecration it is Christ’s body; old creature made new — stop before §.IX
english: How can what is bread be Christ’s body by consecration? By the Lord’s words the sacrament is made — Christ’s speech is operative.

If bread and wine begin to be what they were not and are changed into another, then it was not Christ’s body before consecration, but after it is. He spoke and it was done: you were an old creature; after consecration you begin to be a new one.
Stop before §.IX (fifth century: Chrysostom and Augustine).

title: Annotatio IV §.IX open: Fifth century — Chrysostom and Augustine as chief witnesses
english: §.IX: for the FIFTH century — last of the purer Evangelical ages — many Fathers could be cited, but two snatch the palm.
East and West’s doctors par excellence: Chrysostom and Augustine.

title: Annotatio IV §.IX: Chrysostom Hom. 45 — mysteries spiritually; intelligible gift of body and blood
english: Chrysostom (Hom. 45 on John) strips carnality from the mysteries and from the Supper’s carnal presence and participation.

Mysteries are for interior eyes — spiritual. As baptism’s sensible water carries an intelligible regeneration-gift, so the intelligible gift of body and blood is received by faith’s spiritual intelligence, not by bodily action.

title: Annotatio IV §.IX: Augustine (1) — Institution words figurative; metonymy; Doctr. Chr. 2.16
english: Augustine (1): the essential Institution words (‘Take, eat, This is my Body’) are figurative — not without metonymy (Against Adimantus 12; Doctr. Chr. 2.16).
If a command seems to order a crime, it is figurative: ‘Unless you eat my flesh…’ seems criminal — therefore it is a FIGURE commanding communion in the Passion and memory of the crucified flesh.

title: Annotatio IV §.IX: Augustine (2–3) — figure does not remove true presence; presence and participation spiritual
english: Augustine (2): the figure does not remove true presence or participation — Christians celebrate with sacrosanct oblation and participation of Body and blood (Against Faustus 20.18).
(3) Presence and participation are spiritual: understand spiritually; the sacrament understood spiritually quickens (Ps. 98). Tract. 25 John: Why prepare teeth and belly? Believe, and you have eaten.

title: Annotatio IV §.IX: Augustine (4) — exclude local presence and oral handling; body in one place
english: Augustine (4): local presence and oral handling shut out — until the age ends the Lord is above, yet His Truth is here with us.

The Lord’s risen body must be in ONE PLACE; His truth is everywhere. Absent yet present: body in heaven, Majesty not withdrawn. We cannot handle Him in heaven with hand or mouth — only touch by Faith.

title: Annotatio IV §.IX close: Augustine (5) — unworthy excluded; disciples ate the Lord, Judas the Lord’s bread — stop before §.X
english: Augustine (5): the unworthy (impenitent, unbelieving) are excluded from participation of the Body.
Disciples ate the bread the Lord; Judas ate the Lord’s bread against the Lord (Tract. 59 on John).
Stop before §.X (sixth century onward — decline; Gelasius still holding).

title: Annotatio IV §.X open: Sixth century — end of better ages; Christian truth begins to decline
english: §.X: we have reached the end of the better ages and the start of the worse — the SIXTH — when Christian truth began to rush downhill.
Mejerus opens his sixth section (Christian Religion of the sixth age, p. 164) with that framing.

title: Annotatio IV §.X: Mejerus — six ages; sixth accelerates errors and superstitions
english: Mejerus: Age V still good; IV better; the first three best — then ages follow in which Christianity puts on a new, worse face.
Six ages from the Church’s beginnings to the Reformation: errors creep in the first five; in the sixth they rush in faster and openly.

title: Annotatio IV §.X: Yet some hold Eucharistic truth — Gelasius (near-first papal name)
english: Yet even in this age some clung more constantly to Eucharistic truth.
Among them GELASIUS — almost first of the papal name and dignity — in a writing against Eutyches and Nestorius (Gratian, de Consecrat. Dist. 2 c. 12), for truth and against Transubstantiation.

title: Annotatio IV §.X: Gelasius — divina res; bread and wine substance remains; imago et similitudo
english: Gelasius: the Sacraments of Christ’s body and blood that we take are a DIVINE THING — through them we share the divine nature.
Yet bread and wine do not cease to be in substance and nature; in the Mysteries’ action the IMAGE AND LIKENESS of body and blood are celebrated.

title: Annotatio IV §.X: Foecundus Hermianensis — improper speech; spiritual presence; mystery contains
english: Foecundus of Hermiane (same age; Justinian’s time) seconds Gelasius: Christ’s words are improper speech; presence in the Eucharist is spiritual.

We call the sacrament in consecrated bread and cup His body and blood — not that bread is PROPERLY body or cup blood, but that they contain the MYSTERY — following Vigilius of Trent on the body’s natural local absence on earth.

title: Annotatio IV §.X close: Vigilius — natural local absence; two natures — stop before §.XI
english: Vigilius (against Eutyches and Nestorius) states the Reformers’ sentence: according to humanity the Son withdrew; according to divinity He is with us.

By the servant-form taken into heaven He is ABSENT; by the form of God He is present on earth. Flesh once on earth was not in heaven; now in heaven it is NOT ON EARTH. One Christ of BOTH NATURES — everywhere by divinity, place-bound by humanity.
Stop before §.XI (seventh century; Isidore).

title: Annotatio IV §.XI open: Seventh century — Mejerus; few truth-witnesses; sterile age
english: §.XI: what hope for the SEVENTH age confirming Eucharistic truth? Mejerus puts it in the open.

Protestant doctors refer Anti-Christ’s beginnings (East and West) to this age — East: ruin of whole religion; West: Rome drives the Church toward servitude. Truth-witnesses few; Age VII sterile of good writers.

title: Annotatio IV §.XI: Isidore de Offic. — bread/wine called body/blood; into sacrament not substance
english: So Strimesius summons one alone: ISIDORE of Seville (de Offic. Eccles. 1.8).

Bread is called Christ’s body because it confirms ours; wine referred to His blood because it works blood in the flesh — visible things that, sanctified, pass INTO THE SACRAMENT OF THE DIVINE BODY (not into the substance of body and blood).

title: Annotatio IV §.XI: Isidore Etymolog. — participation of faith; words expunged, Bertram preserved
english: Clearer still (Etymolog. 6.12): visible bread and wine nourish the outer man; Christ’s word, the living bread, recreates faithful souls THROUGH THE PARTICIPATION OF FAITH.
Those words are struck from today’s printed Isidore — preserved by Bertram the Presbyter (John of Durham notes).

title: Annotatio IV §.XI: Bede — sacrament in FIGURE of bread and wine; figure at the Supper
english: Next to Isidore: the VENERABLE BEDE (British Isles’ doctor; name famous mainly in the eighth age).

On Ps. 22: in place of the lamb’s flesh and blood Christ put the Sacrament of His flesh and blood in the FIGURE of bread and wine. On Ps. 3: at the Supper He gave the disciples the FIGURE of His sacrosanct body and blood.

title: Annotatio IV §.XI: Bede — left church CORPORALITER; goes as man, remains as God
english: Bede also seriously detests the falsehood of a corporal presence of Christ or His body — on earth or in the Sacred Supper.

Ascending Victor after the resurrection He left the Church CORPORALLY, yet never without divine presence. As man He went; as God He remained — going as in one place, remaining as everywhere (Mark 4.13; John 14).

title: Annotatio IV §.XI close: Bede John 6 — eat SPIRITUALLY spiritual food — stop before §.XII
english: On John 6: whoever would live, believe in Christ and eat SPIRITUALLY the SPIRITUAL FOOD — the incorporeal of Christ’s body — and not be a putrid member.
Stop before §.XII (eighth century; Damascene / image-age).

title: Annotatio IV §.XII open: Eighth century — Mejerus age of wrath; images and Eucharistic mutation
english: §.XII: the EIGHTH age — with the Seventh, Mejerus’s age of divine wrath — is infamous for defending images in temples and for mutating Eucharistic truth into falsehood.
Bread and wine into Body and Blood, each propped on false reason and human wisdom, plus many mortal inventions in doctrine and rites (Spanheim, Hist. Imag.).

title: Annotatio IV §.XII: Rom 1 applied — glory of God exchanged for images and bread-foam
english: So far that Paul’s charge against the Gentiles (Romans) fits most of this age’s Christian Church:

Knowing God they did not glorify Him; claiming to be wise they became fools and exchanged the glory of the incorruptible God for fashioned images of every kind — and the foam of bread for posterity to adore.

title: Annotatio IV §.XII: Damascene — images champion; bread/wine COMMUTANTUR into body and blood
english: John of Damascus, that age’s chief Doctor of Orthodoxy, fought sharply for images (Calvisius/Helvisus note ~728–730) — and turned toward (or rather preluded) Pontifical errors on the Eucharist.

Orthodox Faith 4.4: as bread and wine naturally change into the eater’s body, so the bread, wine, and water of the proposition are supernaturally CHANGED into Christ’s body and blood — Theophylact must emend him (Whittaker).

title: Annotatio IV §.XII: Mejerus — Damascene author of new scholastic method; simple doctrine mutated
english: Guilty also of many later ‘scholastic’ terms rashly thrust into sacred theology — Mejerus names Damascene author of a new scientific method of treating Christian doctrine.

Thorny useless questions; new opinions as dogmas; rare appeal to Scripture; philosopher-formulas over sound words — and followers gradually turned the ancients’ simple doctrine into scholastic disputations.

title: Annotatio IV §.XII: Orthodox opposition — Constantinople; FIGURE OF CHRIST’S BODY vs all images
english: Meanwhile truly Orthodox (Scripture-clinging) opposed Damascene’s flood of errors in the same Eighth age.

Gathered at Constantinople (fifth / Greeks’ seventh Oecumenical; Copronymus and Leo Isaurian — Spanheim vindicates them): by the FIGURE OF CHRIST’S BODY they set in the Supper they tried to abolish every sacred use of images.

title: Annotatio IV §.XII close: Irene’s Nicaean iconolaters — bread itself body by conversion — stop before §.XIII
english: Under worst Irene they met heaviest contradiction from Nicaean Iconolaters, who contend the Supper bread is not the Figure of the Body but Christ’s body itself by Conversion (see Annotat. 3 §.3).
Stop before §.XIII (ninth century; Charlemagne / Bertram reclaiming).

title: Annotatio IV §.XIII open: Ninth century — reclaimers against both Transubstantiations; Charlemagne FIGURE
english: §.XIII: though Nicaean sentences on image-transmutation and bread-into-Body held first place until the Reformation, the NINTH age still found reclaimers against both Transubstantiations.

Around its entrance CHARLES THE GREAT restrained image-veneration (Frankfurt 794) and, to Alcuin, said Christ gave bread and cup in the FIGURE of His body and blood — a great Sacrament for our profit.

title: Annotatio IV §.XIII: Charles the Bald commissions Bertram and Erigena on Lord’s body and blood
english: Mid-century: CHARLES THE BALD, eager for Evangelical truth on the Eucharist, ordered Bertram the Presbyter and Erigena the Scot to write treatises on the Lord’s body and blood.
Bertram’s still circulates among the learned — Strimesius draws propositions that illustrate the Eucharistic truth.

title: Annotatio IV §.XIII: Bertram (1) — Institution words improper; bread and wine exist FIGURATE; memory of Passion
english: Bertram (1): Institution words are improper — bread and wine exist FIGURATIVELY as Christ’s body and blood.

Named body and blood, they represent the memory of the Lord’s Passion; set on the altar in the FIGURE or memory of His death, so present memory of what was done may make us partakers of the divine gift.

title: Annotatio IV §.XIII: Bertram — natural body not corporally present; SIGNUM and SPECIES vs truth; deny oral eating only
english: Bertram (II): Christ’s natural body is not present in the Supper in a corporal mode — what ministers handle differs from the glorified body; the Eucharistic bread is SIGN and SPECIES, that is the truth itself (pledge vs thing; image vs reality).
He does not deny truth taken in the sacrament — souls are fed with Spiritual food and drink — he denies only that the true natural body is eaten with the body’s Mouth.

title: Annotatio IV §.XIII: Bertram — not corporal/oral eating; spiritual presence and participation (SPIRITUALE CORPUS)
english: Bertram (III): the body born of Mary, dead, risen, at the Father’s right, is not what teeth press and throats swallow daily — that corporal intake does not supply eternal life.

(IV) Yet he confesses Spiritual presence and participation: bread and wine pass into something better not CORPORALLY but SPIRITUALLY — under corporal covering the SPIRITUAL BODY AND BLOOD are actually present; SPIRITUAL FOOD and DRINK.

title: Annotatio IV §.XIII close: Erigena coeval truth; Amalarius / Rabanus / Walafrid — stop before §.XIV
english: Erigena, Bertram’s coeval fellow summoned by Charles the Bald, stated the same Eucharistic truth — his treatise lost (or burned by hostile zeal), but On the Division of Nature (Oxford recovery) and other writings make faith.
See also Amalarius, Rabanus Maurus, Walafrid Strabo, and Bertram himself vindicated in Durham pp. 88–97. Stop before §.XIV (tenth century).

title: Annotatio IV §.XIV open: Tenth century — Baronius/Bellarmine dark age; yet genuine Supper witnesses
english: §.XIV: Baronius marks the TENTH age with black coal — iron for sterility of good, leaden for overflowing evil, obscure for want of writers.
Bellarmine’s cry: unhappy age — no illustrious writers, no councils, pontiffs little solicitous for the ecclesiastical republic.

title: Annotatio IV §.XIV: Cosin — Erigerus’s witnesses; English homilies parallel to Bertram
english: Yet it still had professors and witnesses of a genuine Supper explanation, collected by Erigerus of Louvain.
Cosin (English bishop) brings into the midst English homilies once read publicly in churches — words at p. 98 exactly parallel to Bertram.

title: Annotatio IV §.XIV: Paschal Homily — suffered body vs host; SPIRITUALE CORPUS; pledge and FIGURE
english: Paschal Homily: much difference between the body in which Christ suffered and the body consecrated in the host.

The suffered body has Mary’s flesh, blood, bones, soul; the SPIRITUAL BODY we call Host is from many grains, without blood or soul — temporal, chewable; the Mystery is pledge and FIGURE; Christ’s body is the truth itself.

title: Annotatio IV §.XIV: Paschal Homily — what is seen is bread; spiritually understood is Life
english: The Homily hinge: eyes meet bread.
Faith understanding meets Life — spiritual reading of the same host.

title: Annotatio IV §.XIV: Wulfinus Homily — host Christ’s body not CORPORALITER but SPIRITUALITER
english: Bishop Wulfinus’s Homily, brief but sinewy: the sacramental Host is Christ’s body not CORPORALLY but SPIRITUALLY.
Not the body in which Christ suffered, but the body of which He spoke when He consecrated bread and wine into the host.

title: Annotatio IV §.XIV close: true real presence in spiritual mode (John 6) — stop before §.XV
english: These words inculcate both true real presence in the Sacred Supper and the sole genuine mode Christ defined in John 6 — the spiritual.
The Homily’s close does not deny real presence of the suffered body — only corporal presence opposed to the spiritual. Stop before §.XV (Hildebrandine / Berengar).

title: Annotatio IV §.XV open: Eleventh century — Hildebrandine age; papal tyranny at its summit
english: §.XV: the ELEVENTH age is commonly called Hildebrandine — most infamous by Pope Hildebrand (Gregory VII)’s malice and tyranny.
Papal dominion, born full under Boniface III (Phocas, Age VII), was driven to its summit by Hildebrandine arts and his insolent Dictates.

title: Annotatio IV §.XV: Hildebrand involves Berengar of Tours, century’s chief Eucharistic confessor
english: As Hildebrand’s tyranny raged against the Emperors — especially Henry IV — so it also involved that age’s most celebrated Eucharistic confessor.
BERENGAR OF TOURS — though for another cause.

title: Annotatio IV §.XV: Writings destroyed — figure/type/sign language under pressure; yet adhered to truth
english: His exact modes of speaking on the Sacred Supper are hard to pin down: enemies thoroughly suppressed and deleted his writings.

Under Transubstantiators’ pressure he more often stressed Figure, Type, and Sign than Antitype and Christ’s most-present Body — yet as to the thing and substance he firmly held the truth, even if adversaries’ cruelty sometimes made him look merely human.

title: Annotatio IV §.XV: Fulbert of Chartres — mystery by SPIRIT OF FAITH; interior taste of bread of life
english: Consensus with the truth is clear from his teacher Fulbert of Chartres and from writings that oppose and review his sentence.

Fulbert to Adeodatus: look on the Eucharist’s faith-mystery not with bodily sight but by the SPIRIT OF FAITH — outwardly bread and wine, inwardly Body and Blood; taste by interior affection; take the bread of life as the interior man’s food.

title: Annotatio IV §.XV: Lanfranc quotes Berengar — sacrament does not cease what it was; visible sign, invisible res
english: Among opposing books, Lanfranc of Canterbury On the Truth of the Lord’s Body stands out — and repeats Berengar’s own words.

By altar consecration bread and wine become a Sacrament of Religion yet do not cease what they were; the Church’s sacrifice is visible sacrament plus invisible res (Christ’s body); sacraments are visible seals — the invisible things are what is honored.

title: Annotatio IV §.XV close: not consubstantiation patron — Rupert charges bare sign; more in Annot. 3 — stop
english: Some wrongly make Berengar a consubstantiation patron — even Rupert of Deutz (crasser consubstantiation’s chief author) refuses that and instead charges him with wanting a bare sign of the sacred thing.
Rupert attacks truth-confessors as having no argument but that bare-sign claim (ascribed also to Augustine). Rest on Berengar: see above, Annot. 3. Stop before §.XVI / next extract.
